styleNotes: British English spelling throughout (fulfilment, colour, organise, catalogue, authorised); money in £, dates like '21 October 2026', 24-hour or '2pm' times.
Company is always 'Provida', never 'Provida UK'. Keep system names capitalised exactly: Syrinx, Papertrail, Conduit, Trengo, ERPNext, Stockup, COSHH.
Teams chat with colleagues is very casual: mostly lowercase, no full stops, trailing '...', shorthand lmk, kk, np, tyvm, mb, idk, tbh, lol, 'u', 'mtg'.
Nicknames: Mo (Mojola), Phil (Philip), GG (Graham Gilbert), HWG (himself); calls Neil 'Dad' when writing to staff.
Internal emails open 'Hi Mojola and Lavinia,', 'Hey Mo,', 'Morning Mo,', 'Afternoon Lavinia,' or 'Hello All,' and close 'Thanks,' + 'Harley'. Friendly emoji (😊 🙂) are common.
External emails (suppliers, Trengo, IT provider, UBT) are polite and short in full sentences, closing 'Kind regards,' or 'Best,' + 'Harley'.
Uses a hyphen with a trailing space as a dash ('yet- does this make sense?', 'btw', 'FYI-'); rarely types em dashes himself.
Staff updates are plain and practical: a short title, what changed, numbered or bulleted steps, concrete numbers and percentages, and what staff must do.
Product codes, SKUs and part numbers stay uppercase and unspaced exactly as written (H060EXYEL, DIS015, RJCON6P6C, PV210).
Phone replies (Outlook for Android) are one or two quick, informal sentences; self-corrections are flagged with 'Sorry-' or '*' and 'mb'.
